open_points.subject: open_store
open_points.text: then open the database file inside data_directory as the module's one SQLite connection with synchronous FULL, after os.lstat finds that path no symbolic link;
open_points.other_text: Every file and directory the module creates inside data_directory — the database file and its journal, the content-addressed area, the spool area, each run's spool directory, every temporary and every published file — MUST be created owned by the process's effective user and granting no permission to group or others, so that the privacy check of the next start passes on the kernel's own files (A18 rule 2).
open_points.question: Must open_store support an absent database file by treating os.lstat's FileNotFoundError as an acceptable non-link result, or is the database now required to exist even though the module is required to create it?

open_points.subject: open_store
open_points.text: then open the database file inside data_directory as the module's one SQLite connection with synchronous FULL, after os.lstat finds that path no symbolic link;
open_points.other_text: Every file and directory under the data directory MUST be opened without following symbolic links; a symbolic link met by any call after start makes that call raise StoreInternalError with nothing written.
open_points.question: Must the database still be opened with a no-follow guarantee in addition to the preceding os.lstat check, or is the non-atomic lstat check intended to replace that requirement?
